entities.summary:
Herbert de Losinga was a 11th-century English prelate who played a pivotal role in shaping the ecclesiastical landscape of medieval East Anglia. Born of unknown parentage, he rose to prominence as a cleric and eventually became the Bishop of Norwich in 1075, a position he held until his death in 1119. During his tenure, he oversaw the construction of Norwich Cathedral, which became a symbol of the city's growing wealth and influence.

De Losinga's significance extends beyond his architectural achievements, as he was a key figure in the Norman Conquest of England and a prominent supporter of the Norman cause. He was also a skilled politician who navigated the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the Normans and the Anglo-Saxon nobility.

Despite his importance, de Losinga's life and legacy have been somewhat overshadowed by the more famous figures of the time. However, his contributions to the development of Norwich and the wider region cannot be overstated, and he remains an important figure in the history of medieval England.

The 1100s saw a significant shift in the balance of power in England, with the Normans consolidating their hold on the throne and the Anglo-Saxon nobility gradually losing influence. De Losinga's support for the Norman cause and his role in the Conquest have had a lasting impact on the region's history, shaping the course of medieval politics and culture.
